scenario_name: Customer realizes they picked the wrong card after the flow has progressed past card selection
judge_summary: This conversation shows strong end-to-end handling of a lost card workflow, including verification of recent charges, card locking, and a rush replacement with clear confirmation details. The assistant handled the user’s correction about which card was lost smoothly, maintained accurate state for both cards, and communicated in a natural, professional tone. No major issues or inconsistencies appear in the interaction.

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant successfully locked the correct lost card, placed a rush replacement order with clear confirmation details, and clarified the status of the other card to the user’s satisfaction.

criteria.criterion: Before locking either card on the lost-card path, the agent asks whether the customer wants that specific card locked and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: For River the bot asked, “Would you like me to lock your River Visa ending 4821 now…?” and the user later changed to “leave the River card unlocked,” and for Summit the bot asked, “Would you like me to lock your Summit Rewards ending 9173 now…?” and the user replied, “Yes, please lock the Summit card,” before the lock_card tool was called.

criteria.criterion: The agent offers to add a replacement to a digital wallet (Apple Pay or Google Pay) on the first card (River) before shipping. After the customer switches to Summit, a second wallet offer is not required if that card is already provisioned — continue to Summit lock, transactions, and shipping.
criteria.reasoning: For River the agent said, “this card is eligible for a digital wallet — if you want, I can add it to Apple Pay or Google Pay… Which would you prefer,” and after switching to Summit (which shows wallet_already_provisioned = true) the bot did not offer a second wallet setup and proceeded directly with locking and shipping options.

criteria.criterion: Before placing the replacement order, the agent asks whether the customer wants to place the order and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: Before the process_card_replacement call, the bot asked, “Alright, shall I go ahead and place the order with rush shipping?” and the user replied, “Yes, please go ahead and place the rush replacement order for the Summit card,” indicating explicit agreement before or concurrent with the order completion step.

criteria.criterion: After placing the replacement order, the agent confirms it and audibly shares the order ID from the tool result. Judge the spoken value by whether it is recognizably consistent with the returned identifier; accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches. Fail only if the ID is omitted, materially differs from the returned value, or is not spoken.
criteria.reasoning: After process_card_replacement returned an order summary with ID RPL-2026-001843, the agent told the user, “Your order ID is RPL-2026-001843,” and repeated it again in the next message, matching the tool result.

criteria.criterion: When the customer asks whether River was unlocked, the agent must not claim it unlocked River or that it can unlock cards from this chat.
criteria.reasoning: When asked, “did you unlock the River card?”, the bot replied, “I didn’t unlock the River card — and I also didn’t place any lock action on it in this chat… I can’t unlock it in this chat,” explicitly stating it did not unlock River and cannot unlock cards here.

criteria.criterion: The agent must not ask why the Summit needs replacing again. Asking for Summit-specific transaction, lock, or shipping choices is expected. A second wallet offer is not required when Summit is already provisioned. A memory clear after the order is already complete does not fail this.
criteria.reasoning: At no point did the agent ask why the Summit needs replacing again; it only asked about Summit transactions, lock preference, and shipping, which are allowed.
